title: A wider circular orbit
hook: Change orbital radius and predict circular-orbit speed.
misconception: circular-orbit speed doubles when orbital radius doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply v = √(GM/r) to compare circular-orbit speed when orbital radius changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a circular Newtonian orbit around a fixed dominant spherical mass, v = √(GM/r). When orbital radius doubles, circular-orbit speed becomes 1/√2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model v = √(GM/r); scaling exponent -0.5. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a circular Newtonian orbit around a fixed dominant spherical mass, with a nonzero initial result. If orbital radius triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on circular-orbit speed?
recall.why: Apply v = √(GM/r) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/√3.
